text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT SALE - Philippine firms bought 35,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat for February shipment, traders said. The purchase was said to comprise 29,000 tonnes of dark northern spring wheat at $3.94 per bushel FOB and 6,000 tonnes of white wheat at $3.90 per bushel.
- Two S. Korean firms bought 21,500 tonnes of U.S. wheat from Mitsubishi of Japan, traders said. Shipment was slated for March 5 to April 5.

WHEAT TENDERS - Jordan will tender on February 5 for 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat or equivalent origin for shipment by the end of March, traders said. U.S. wheat would be covered under the GSM 102 program, traders said.

Private Moroccan importers will purchase a total of 27,000 tonnes of optional-origin milling wheat this week, grain traders said. One tender for 12,000 tonnes is set January 21, with delivery slated for January 31. A second tender will be held for 15,000 tonnes on January 23. Shipment for that purchase is set for February 25 through March 5, traders and export sources said.
WHEAT TENDER -Lebanon's economy ministry plans to buy 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard wheat later this month, the government said.

- New was awaited on Bangladesh's tender for 100,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 wheat or Australian standard or better Canadian winter red/spring wheat for shipment by February 21. The tender closed on January 18, and results were expected two to three days later.
CORN TENDER - News was awaited on South Africa's Maize Board's tender for 15,000 tonnes of yellow maize for either export or domestic use. The offer was seen closing January 16.

- Taiwan Feed group will tender Tuesday for a 54,000-tonne shipment of U.S. No. 2 corn. Shipment from the U.S. Gulf was set for March 8 to March 22 or from the Pacific Northwest between March 23 and April 6, traders said.

CORN AND SOYBEAN TENDERS - Taiwan Sugar Corp will tender for a combined 30,000-tonne U.S. corn and soybean cargo on Tuesday, traders said. The shipment will consist of 20,000 tonnes of corn and 10,000 tonnes of soybeans. Shipment will be for February 25 to March 10 delivery from the U.S. Gulf or March 10 to March 25 from the Pacific Northwest.
RICE TENDER - Syria's General Foreign Trade Organization for Chemicals and Foodstuffs is seeking to buy 12,000 tonnes of white rice for March shipment. Results would be February 13.

MARKET TALK - Saudi Arabian traders are seeking to buy rice from the U.S., Australia and Ecuador after a 30 percent increase in Indian and Pakistani rice prices, a Saudi newspaper said on Monday. Saudi Arabia imports around 700,000 tonnes of rice a year, mostly from India, the United States, Thailand and Pakistan at a cost of around three billion riyals ($800 million).

MARKET TALK - Taiwanese grain and oilseeds buyers have shown strong interest in buying up to 272,500 tonnes of soybeans and 136,000 tonnes of corn to lock in supplies at current levels ahead of an anticipated increase in world prices, traders said.

- Five South Korean companies have bought 24,000 tonnes of Chinese corn through a private negotiation, traders said. Traders said 12,000 tonnes was sold at $145 per tonne C and F for arrival March 10 and the remaining 12,000 tonnes at $142 C and F per tonne for arrival on April 5.

- Iraq is seen deciding on Monday on a tender for 100,000 tonnes of French wheat in March and April, traders said. Exporters also expected Iraq to end up buying more wheat from France, possibly as much as 300,000 to 350,000 tonnes.
